caption:
Somewhere in the middle of the Atlantic lie two Portuguese archipelagos — Madeira and the Azores 🌍

Many people are surprised to learn that this remote-looking place is actually part of Europe and surprisingly easy to reach. Yet even in the middle of the travel season, it’s still possible to stand on a cliff, hike a trail, or watch the ocean with the feeling that it’s just you and nature.

This video includes drone views from Madeira, São Miguel, Flores, Corvo, São Jorge, and Terceira — islands where dramatic landscapes, volcanic mountains, waterfalls, and endless ocean create one of the most unique corners of Europe.

I’ve been living on these islands for more than three and a half years, and almost every week I still discover something new. Hidden viewpoints, quiet trails, remote waterfalls, beautiful beaches, and small places most travelers never find.

🗺️ To make exploring easier, I’ve gathered my favorite locations into INTERACTIVE TRAVEL GUIDES & MAPS.
They include the best hikes, viewpoints, beaches, waterfalls, hotels, restaurants, and activities — everything that helps turn a trip into a well-planned adventure.

📲 The guides work inside an offline-friendly mobile app with a map, so you can easily navigate even if you didn’t plan your trip in advance.

5 of our favorite kid-friendly activities in Tokyo that honestly blew me away as a mom traveling with littles 🇯🇵✨

1️⃣ Comme’N KIDS at Azabudai Hills — a kids-only bakery where little shoppers go in solo and buy their own treats while we cheer from the doorway.

3️⃣ teamLab Planets TOKYO — an immersive art world that had all three of my kids in total awe. Barefoot water floors, floating orchids, and glowing rooms that react to touch.

4️⃣ Tokyo Disneyland & Tokyo DisneySea — both parks are incredibly toddler-friendly with tons of rides under the height limit, character moments, and unmatched attention to detail.

5️⃣ Family Onsen Time — unwind after busy city days at family-friendly onsens like Thermae‑Yu Shinjuku, Oedo Onsen Monogatari Urayasu Mangekyo, or Hakone Kowakien Yunessun if you’re up for a quick trip out of town.

Tokyo with kids doesn’t just work, it thrives. There’s magic, learning, calm, and chaos all beautifully balanced. Save this for your next trip with littles 🌸

caption:
What if I told you there’s a better way👇 
{free easy flow itinerary below)

Most people see Japan in the wrong order and that’s exactly why so many first trips feel exhausting

Most people plan Japan by cities instead of by distance and rail lines. I know we did on our first trip!
 That’s when itineraries start to feel rushed, disjointed, and unnecessarily tiring

Japan is one of the easiest countries to travel when the flow makes sense

The order that works best for most first-timers👇
Tokyo → Kyoto → Osaka (with Kyoto as your main base)

Why this works
• Tokyo is best tackled first while you’re fresh and adjusting to the time zone
• Kyoto and Osaka are close enough to combine without constant hotel changes
• You can day trip instead of hauling luggage every few days
• Travel days stay short, simple, and predictable

A simple itinerary that actually flows 🇯🇵

✨ Days 1–4: Tokyo Arrive, adjust, and head to neighbourhoods like Shibuya, Shinjuku, and Asakusa 🚂 Optional day trips once settled: Hakone or Kamakura

✨ Days 5–8: Kyoto (base here) Temples and traditional streets
Kiyomizu-dera, Gion (early or at night), Adashino Nenbutsuji, and Pontocho after dark 🚂 Easy day trips from Kyoto: • Nara • Osaka

✨ Days 9–10: Osaka (optional overnight stay)
Move once, stay central, and focus on food, shopping, and nightlife
Dotonbori for the atmosphere, Shinsekai for casual eats, Namba for shopping, and evening bar hopping around Umeda

🚆 Getting between bases (it’s easy)
• Tokyo → Kyoto: Tokaido Shinkansen (around 2–2.5 hours)
• Kyoto → Osaka: JR Special Rapid (around 30 minutes)

This isn’t the only way to do Japan but for first-timers, we’ve found it’s the most forgiving

To park here you have to buy a €40 permit before hand. The time slots to purchase open one month before & I’m sure sell out quickly in peak summer so be prepared. Otherwise it’s a long uphill hike to the start point.

caption:
16 Fun Things To Do in Tokyo Especially With Kids 🇯🇵✨ (Save This!)
Tokyo is incredibly family-friendly — safe, clean & full of magical experiences. 
Here are the best activities with smart tips for each 👇
1.🌊 DisneySea (¥7,900–¥10,900) 
Arrive early. Download official Tokyo Disney Resort app for wait times & show schedules.
2.🏰 Disneyland (¥7,900 - ¥10,900)
Perfect for younger kids. Start with Fantasyland in the morning.
3.⚡ Warner Bros. Studio Tour (¥6,300+ )
Keep 3–4 hours minimum. Stroller friendly.
4.🎀 Sanrio Puroland (¥3,900–¥5,900) 
Indoor theme park, great for Hello Kitty fans & rainy days.
5.✨ TeamLab (¥3,800– ¥4,200)
Wear pants/shorts (mirror floors + water area). Light/white clothes look best in photos.
6.👘 Kimono Experience (in Asakusa)(¥3,000–¥6,000) 
Choose lightweight styles for kids for comfort.
7.🚢 Tokyo Cruise (¥2,000)
Evening gives beautiful skyline views; Pre-book in advance.
8.☕ 2D Café ( ¥770+) in Shin Okubu
Visit during non-peak hours for easier seating.
9.🌇 Shibuya Sky (¥2,700 - ¥3,400) 
Daytime is less crowded with little ones; sunset slots sell out fast.
10.🚡 Air Cabin (Yokohama) (¥1,000) 
Short ropeway ride, easy to combine with a relaxed day trip of Yokohama.
11.🗼 Tokyo Skytree (¥2,100- ¥3100)
 Visit at night for magical city lights. Lots of family-friendly shopping & dining below in mall.
12.🍵 Japanese Tea Ceremony – (¥ 10,000) 
Book short, family-friendly sessions. Check BUB activity centers in Asakusa near Sensoji Temple.
13.⚔ Samurai Experience (¥15,000)
Good options available in BUB activity center in Asakusa area.
14.🐶 Animal Café (¥ 1400 -¥3000) - Rio Dog Cafe, Asakusa 
Dog cafés are generally more kid-friendly. Always supervise children.
15.🍰 Themed / Character Desserts(¥1,000+) 
Many popular dessert spots require reservations.
16. Rickshaw Ride (Asakusa) (¥3,000–¥18,000) 
Fun storytelling + great family photo opportunity.

🇯🇵 Best part?
👧 Under 12 yrs – usually ~50% off
👶 Under 4–5 yrs – often FREE (varies by place)

Tokyo truly has something for every age 🇯🇵✨

caption:
We’ve ridden hundreds of trains in Japan and this is by far the most beautiful one we’ve experienced

But it’s a tricky one to catch

You need to time your trip around the weekend because it only runs a few times each week. If you can coordinate it though, it’s absolutely worth the effort

Let me show you how to do it

🚆 Kyo-Train Garaku
📍 Route
Runs between Kyoto Kawaramachi and Osaka Umeda on the Hankyu Railway line

🗓️ When it runs
This is where most travellers get caught out
The train mainly operates on weekends and public holidays, with only a few departures each day
Typically:
• Kyoto → Osaka: morning services
• Osaka → Kyoto: afternoon services
Because departures are limited, check the timetable before locking in your travel day

✋ Remember to comment TRAIN and we’ll send you the timetable so you can plan it properly

💰 Cost
The best part? You don’t need a special ticket
You can ride the Kyo Train Garaku for the price of a normal Hankyu train fare, about ¥410 (under $5 USD).
No reservations required. Just tap in like a regular train

🧳 Luggage tip
You can bring luggage onboard, but we recommend arriving 30 minutes before departure so you can be at the front of the queue and secure space for your bags

🎟️ Where to catch it
Board at:
• Hankyu Kyoto Kawaramachi Station (Kyoto)
• Hankyu Osaka Umeda Station (Osaka)

✨ Why this train is special
Each carriage is made to reflect a different season in Kyoto with:
• Tatami seating
• Panoramic windows

Trust me when I say you HAVE to ride it!

caption:
Two weeks, four cities, and genuinely the best trip of our lives 🇯🇵✨

We started in Tokyo and stayed at the Keio Plaza Hotel - perfect central location. Beyond what’s in the reel, make sure you hit the Starbucks Tsutaya for the best view of the Shibuya Scramble, explore Shibuya’s incredible sneaker stores, and spend a night bar hopping through Tokyo’s world-class speakeasies. We also loved Senso-ji Temple, the Imperial Palace, and Shinjuku Gyoen Garden.

For Mount Fuji, we drove from Tokyo to Kawaguchiko first, stopped at the Fuji Visitor Centre, then continued to Hakone where we stayed at the Indigo Hotel. The private onsens here were everything. Pro tip: use Japan’s luggage transfer service to ship your bags between cities - you’ll thank me later. We spent two days exploring the Hakone Open Air Museum, taking the Lake Ashi cruise, and riding the ropeway up to Owakudani Valley.

From Hakone, we took the bullet train to Kyoto and stayed at the Fauchon Hotel, close to Gion. This is where the trip really hit different. We wandered through Arashiyama Bamboo Grove (go early!), visited Kinkaku-ji and Fushimi Inari, explored Nishiki Market, and did the kimono tea ceremony which was hands down the highlight of the entire trip. Book it in advance.

We did a day trip to Nara - Todaiji Temple is stunning and the deer park is fun, just protect your snacks because those deer are ruthless 😂
Finally, we drove to Osaka and stayed at the Swissotel Nankai right above the train station. Spent two days shopping and eating before flying home from Osaka Kansai Airport.
Biggest tip? Book experiences and restaurants in advance - Pizza Bar on 38th, the tea ceremony, popular spots - they fill up fast.

Save this for your Japan trip and ask me anything below! 👇

Comment “SWISS” and I’ll send you the ultimate 10 day itinerary for traveling to 🇨🇭Switzerland with kids! 

I have been to Switzerland many times, and this is the exact trip I just took with my own 3 kids (ages 3, 7 & 9) this July! 

This itinerary combines:

🥾Kid-Friendly Hikes
🏔️ Amazing Mountain Views
🚠 Cable Car, Train and Funicular rides
🇨🇭Traditional Swiss culture 
🌳 Tree-lined stolls on lakeside promenades
⛰️Mountain coasters and zip lines 
🛝 The most fun playgrounds

🚢 Boat rides 
🧀🍦Amazing food 
🇮🇹 ☀️Ending in the Sun- Soaked Italian Region of Lugano- so it actually feels like you visited two countries in one! 

I’ve also included: 
🛌Hotel & Rental Recommendations
🧍‍♂️Tours to book 
🚞Transportation/ train pass recommendations

🇨🇭The best 10 day “Switzerland With Kids” itinerary At-A- Glance:

This is the perfect itinerary that combines it all- but I’ve also listed out potential options to change things depending on your family’s interest and how many days you have to spend!

When we went, we also had my parents and some Aunts and Uncles with us… this is truly a great multigenerational trip !

caption:
If you love mountains, these destinations should be at the very top of your travel list ⛰️✨

🇳🇴 Norway – dramatic fjords, towering peaks, and trails some of the most unique hikes in the world. We spent a couple weeks in the Lofotens and it was unreal. 

🇨🇭 Switzerland – the heart of the Alps, where the most beautiful hikes meet charming alpine villages.

🇮🇹 Dolomites, Italy – jagged limestone peaks, dreamy lakes, and some of the most photogenic hikes in Europe. It is easy to get around and just gorgeous. 

🇦🇷 Patagonia, Argentina/Chile – wild, untamed landscapes with some of the best hikes and viewpoints in the world. Our favourite hiking destination. 

🇺🇸 USA – from the Rockies to the Sierra Nevada, the US has so many beautiful mountains. We have not been to all of them but Glacier National Park and the Tetons is top on our list. 

🇨🇦 Canada – we may be bias, but Canada undoubtedly has some of the best hiking in the world.

For more than 4 years living on Madeira, I’ve had the chance to explore some of the most incredible islands in the Atlantic 🇵🇹

Some of these places honestly feel like they’ve come straight out of a Jurassic Park movie — dramatic volcanic landscapes, lush forests, waterfalls, black-sand beaches, and landscapes that barely look real.

Madeira is the island I call home, but the Azores keep bringing me back. What I love most is that every island has its own character and landscapes.

🌱 Madeira — dramatic mountain ridges, world-class hiking trails, lush forests, and breathtaking sunrises above the clouds.

🌋 São Miguel — volcanic lakes, geothermal hot springs, black-sand beaches, and endless green landscapes.

🌊 Flores — spectacular waterfalls, emerald lagoons, and one of the wildest, most untouched islands in Europe.

🐦 Corvo — Portugal’s smallest island, where life slows down and its massive volcanic caldera feels like another planet.

⛰️ Pico — dominated by Portugal’s highest mountain, with dramatic volcanic landscapes, vineyards growing on black lava, and incredible views across the Atlantic.

After years of exploring these islands, I created 🗺️ INTERACTIVE GUIDES to help independent travelers discover them without spending weeks planning.

🔗 You can find them in my bio — or comment “MADEIRA MAP” or “AZORES MAP” and I’ll send you the direct link 👇

caption:
Some of my favorite European cities I’ve solo traveled to as a female traveler 🧳✈️♥️

Traveling alone can feel intimidating at first, but these spots made me feel super safe, peaceful, and honestly just happy to be on my own. If you’re looking for solo travel ideas or wondering where to go, here are some places I’ve been and loved.

In this video I go through:

	•	Lake Lucerne, Switzerland – such a calm place to walk around and take in the views
	•	Wengen, Switzerland – this mountain town is car-free and just feels like a cozy little dream
	•	Interlaken, Switzerland – easy to get around solo and so many things to do
	•	Florence, Italy – I loved the vibe here, plus it’s really walkable and solo-friendly
	•	Lake Como, Italy – more relaxing, but still a great solo spot if you like slow travel

A couple places I haven’t been yet but have heard are safe and great for solo female travel are Copenhagen and Kyoto, Japan — definitely on my list.

Let me know if you’ve solo traveled to any of these or have any other recommendations!

caption:
KYOTO + OSAKA ITINERARY ⬇️ 

Still can’t decide between Kyoto and Osaka?

On our first trip to Japan, we skipped Osaka completely

We assumed it would feel too similar to Tokyo

We were wrong

We ended up booking a completely separate trip back to Japan just to experience Osaka

Now, we almost always fly into Osaka

We fell in love with the food, the nightlife, the neon lights and the cheeky Osakans

But then we made another mistake

We tried to see Kyoto as a day trip from Osaka

The city is way bigger than most first-time visitors realise, and we felt rushed from the minute we arrived

So if you’re wondering how to split your time between Kyoto and Osaka, here’s exactly what I’d do

🍵 KYOTO
My biggest piece of advice? Forget trying to see every temple. Pick 2-3 that genuinely interest you and spend the rest of your time exploring Kyoto’s neighbourhoods

📍 My recommendation: 3 nights
Could you spend 5 nights here? Absolutely. Would I? Probably not. I’d rather spend 3 nights in Kyoto and use those extra days exploring another part of Japan

Don’t miss: • Kiyomizu-dera • Ninenzaka & Sannenzaka • Gion • Pontocho • Arashiyama • Otagi Nenbutsu-ji • Kinkaku-ji • A day trip to Nara

🚆 GETTING BETWEEN KYOTO & OSAKA
Don’t catch the Shinkansen. The JR Special Rapid train takes around 30 minutes and costs around ¥580

If you’re travelling on a weekend, you have to catch the Kyo Train Garaku instead. It’s one of the most beautiful sightseeing trains connecting Kyoto and Osaka

🍜 OSAKA
My biggest piece of advice? Don’t treat Osaka as a sightseeing city. Treat it as an experience city

📍 My recommendation: 3 nights

Don’t miss: • Dotonbori • Hozenji Yokocho • Shinsekai • Tsutenkaku • Namba Yasaka Shrine • Umeda Sky Building • Kuromon Market • Katsuoji Temple (day trip)

And if I only had one takeaway? Kyoto gives you the days. Osaka gives you the nights. Don’t substitue one for the other. If it’s your first trip, you need both

caption:
🇯🇵 Step into the heart of Japan’s timeless beauty — Kyoto 🌸🏯 A city where ancient tradition meets serene nature, every street feels like a scene from a movie. Once the imperial capital for over a thousand years, Kyoto is filled with stunning temples, peaceful gardens, and wooden townhouses that whisper stories of the past 🍃✨.

⛩️ Wander through the endless red torii gates of Fushimi Inari Shrine, explore the golden glow of Kinkaku-ji Temple, and lose yourself in the tranquil charm of Arashiyama’s bamboo forest 🎋🌿. Whether you’re admiring the spring cherry blossoms or the fiery autumn leaves, Kyoto’s beauty changes with every season — and every moment feels magical 🍁🌸.

🍵 Beyond its breathtaking scenery, Kyoto offers the essence of Japanese culture: matcha tea ceremonies, traditional kaiseki dining, and graceful geisha districts like Gion that capture the spirit of old Japan 💫.

Kyoto isn’t just a destination — it’s an experience that connects you to Japan’s soul. A city that blends elegance, history, and nature so perfectly that every traveler falls in love with it from the very first step 🌍❤️.

caption:
27 in japan wasn’t what i planned. nothing about this year was what i planned.

there’s this version of my life i had mapped out. the one where by now i’d be settled. planning a future with someone. and somewhere along the way i started measuring every birthday against that version instead of the one i’m actually in. LOL 

what the video doesn’t show is the hour before i filmed this. sitting on a hotel bed in tokyo trying to figure out why i felt guilty for being happy.

solo travel changes you in ways that are hard to explain without sounding like a bumper sticker. japan specifically rewired something. 30 days. a lot of convenience store meals. a few very public cries. and somewhere in all of it, the version of my life i was supposed to be living started to feel a lot less real.

i’m 27. i’m somewhere in japan with an oversized carry on. and for the first time in a long time, that’s enough.

save this for the next time your brain tells you you’re behind.

caption:
I took my family to Japan and skipped Tokyo.

And honestly? I'd do it again.

Our last Japan trip was based entirely in Osaka and it ended up being one of our favourite family trips yet.

If you're planning Japan with kids, here are my top Osaka tips:

📍 Stay in Umeda, Namba or Shinsekai for easy transport and plenty of food options

🐠 Don't miss the aquarium, Osaka Kids Plaza, Osaka Castle Playground and the epic mountain slider playground

🚆 Use Osaka as your base for day trips to Kyoto, Kobe and Himeji

🌃 If you have more time, consider an overnight trip to Nagoya or Hiroshima

The biggest surprise? We never felt like we were missing out by skipping Tokyo.

Don't get me wrong...Tokyo is amazing. But if you're travelling with kids, Osaka deserves way more attention than it gets.

Comment ITINERARY and I'll send you my Japan itineraries covering Tokyo, Osaka, Kyoto and Nagoya 🇯🇵

caption:
Tokyo Diaries – Day 1 🇯🇵 @oysheekarimbil @illishakarimbil 

1️⃣ Tokyo Sky Observatory – Oyshee was busy spotting famous landmarks from way up high, while Illisha pressed her little face against the glass, fascinated by the “tiny cars” below.
2️⃣ Meiji Shrine – Oyshee whispered wishes at the shrine, soaking in the calm, while Illisha toddled along the gravel paths chasing sunlight and leaves.
3️⃣ Sensoji Temple – Oyshee loved the colorful market streets, stopping to peek at every stall, while Illisha clapped along to the temple drums and giggled at the lanterns.
4️⃣ Shibuya Crossing – Oyshee was thrilled by the crowd’s perfect chaos, weaving through like a pro, while Illisha held on tight, her eyes wide with amazement at the flashing lights.
5️⃣ Hachiko Statue at Shibuya Station – Oyshee posed with a big smile, proud her name comes from a Japanese word, while Illisha reached out to “pat” Hachiko like a real dog.

These two little explorers made Tokyo even more magical — from giggles to wide-eyed wonder, they turned every stop into a memory. Thank you @yogitaa.mandavkar for tagging along with us for this beautiful Tokyo sojourn 

And this is just the beginning… Tokyo Part 2 will be even better 😉🎌 and hopefully @yadunathkarimbil joining us in some pics😜📸🤩

Lisbon, tailored to your travel style.

🇵🇹 Romance → Alfama — medieval lanes & candlelit fado. Stay: Palácio Belmonte

🇵🇹 Nightlife → Bairro Alto — tiny bars & late nights. Go: Rua da Atalaia

🇵🇹 Food → Cais do Sodré — seafood, petiscos & natural wine. Eat: Taberna da Rua das Flores

🇵🇹 Wine → Palmela & Setúbal — vineyards just beyond Lisbon. Taste: José Maria da Fonseca

🇵🇹 Art & Culture → Chiado — galleries, theatres & literary history. Visit: Museu Nacional de Arte Contemporânea

🇵🇹 Sunset Views → Santa Catarina — Tagus views & local energy. Book: Lisbon Sail sunset cruise

🇵🇹 Hidden Gem → Tapada das Necessidades — wild gardens behind royal walls. Explore: Jardim dos Cactos

🇵🇹 Nature → Monsanto Forest Park — Lisbon’s green lung. Do: Rota da Água, a 7.8 km forest loop

🇵🇹 History → Mouraria — Moorish roots & fado history. Book: Lisbon Art & Soul’s Mouraria tour

🇵🇹 Wellness → Estrela — leafy streets & beautiful gardens. Do: Jardim da Estrela

🇵🇹 Photography → Senhora do Monte — sweeping views over Lisbon. Shoot: sunrise from the miradouro

🇵🇹 Affordable Escape → Arroios — creative, multicultural & local. Eat: Rua Angelina Vidal

🇵🇹 Shopping → Avenida da Liberdade — Lisbon’s luxury boulevard. Shop: flagship boutiques

🇵🇹 Street Art → Marvila — galleries, breweries & industrial murals. Explore: Marvila Art District

🇵🇹 Tram Ride → Tram 28 — Lisbon’s iconic wooden tram. Do: start in Campo de Ourique

🇵🇹 Fado → Alfama — intimate tascas & Lisbon’s signature sound. Hear: Clube de Fado

🇵🇹 Day Trips → Cascais — Atlantic glamour & sandy coves. Book: Cascais coastal tour

🇵🇹 Beach Days → Costa da Caparica — wide Atlantic beaches. Do: book a day at Praia da Morena

🇵🇹 Surfing → Carcavelos — Lisbon’s easiest surf escape. Book: Lisbon Surfaris

2. Altitude: At an elevation of approximately 335 meters (1,100 feet) above sea level, it provides a unique vantage point to admire Madeira's diverse topography. ⛰️

3. Lush Gardens: Immerse yourself in the beauty of the landscaped gardens surrounding Miradouro Pico dos Barcelos. It's the perfect place to relax and take in the scenery. 🌺

4. Sunset Magic: Capture the romance of a Madeira sunset! 🌅 This spot is a photographer's dream and a perfect setting for couples seeking a memorable moment.

6. Easy Access: Whether you're driving or using public transportation, getting to this viewpoint is a breeze, making it a must-visit for tourists and locals alike. 🚗🚋

7. A Piece of History: Miradouro Pico dos Barcelos also holds historical significance, named after João Gonçalves Zarco, one of Madeira's early Portuguese explorers. 🗺️

caption:
8 days exploring the best of California National Parks as a family👇

One of our most favourite road trips in the WORLD!

START: Pick up your hire car in San Francisco and spend 8 days (minimum) visiting 5 epic, world-class national parks before flying out of Los Angeles!

🌿2 NIGHTS - YOSEMITE NATIONAL PARK: The tallest waterfall in North America, the largest granite monolith on Earth and trails taking you to the base of both. 

🌿1 NIGHT - KINGS CANYON: Deepest canyon in the US. The scenic byway to Cedar Grove is one of the most dramatic drives in the US.

🌿1 NIGHT - SEQUOIA NATIONAL PARK: The largest living thing on earth. Panoramic views of the Sierra Nevada. Drive through a fallen sequoia! (Pairs perfectly with Kings canyon as they share an entrance)

🌿2 NIGHTS - DEATH VALLEY: The most extreme landscape on the planet and lowest point in North America. Salt flats, sand dunes at sunrise and artist palette!

🌿2 NIGHTS - JOSHUA TREE: Two deserts colliding and the result is as if you’re on another planet. Giant boulders, cartoon trees and a certified International Dark Sky Park = epic stargazing! 

‼️MUST KNOW‼️
✨Buy the America the Beautiful Pass ($80 USD — covers all 5 parks)
✨ Book Yosemite 6+ months ahead, no exceptions
✨ Avoid Death Valley in summer — temps hit 50°C. Spring or autumn only.
✨ Total driving: around 10 hrs spread across 8 days
✨ Best direction: north to south, SF to LA

.

caption:
Here’s a 3-day itinerary to inspire you for that Osaka trip! 🙌🏯

Day 1
🏯 Explore the famous Osaka Castle
Starting with the iconic landmark! Spend time exploring the museum within, and then enjoy a stroll around the beautiful castle grounds.

🍢 Eat your heart out in Dotonbori
Head to Dotonbori for a guided tour of famous Osakan foods such as takoyaki and kushikatsu. This is a great family-friendly option and also a great way to avoid the crowded nighttime streets. Link in bio!

🐠 Rainy day option: visit the world's largest aquarium
If the weather isn't cooperating for a visit to the castle, why not go to Kaiyukan, one of the world's largest aquariums? Open until 8pm, this Osaka aquarium is a fun way to observe Japan's marine life.

Day 2
🪄Spend the day at Universal Studios Osaka
Home to Super Nintendo World, the Wizarding World of Harry Potter, and the Minion Park, Universal Studios truly has something for everyone, regardless of age. 

🥢 Try one of Osaka's signature dishes: okonomiyaki
Okonomiyaki is a cabbage pancake of sorts, with different toppings and drenched in a blend of savory sauces. One of Osaka's beloved dishes, it's a must-try while in the city. Line up at Okonomiyaki Chitose, one of the top-rated okonomiyaki restaurants, for a delicious lunch or dinner.

🌌 Have an immersive experience at teamLabs Osaka
This botanical garden boasts stunning art installations that will make everyone on your social media feed jealous! Just be sure to book tickets ahead of time.

Day 3
🏯 Gain good luck at Namba Yasaka Shrine
If there's one shrine you should visit while in Osaka, it's Namba Yasaka Shrine. The lion head building is said to chase away evil spirits, leaving visitors with good luck after leaving.

🛍️ Shop away at Shinsaibashi
At 600 meters, Shinsaibashi has everything you may need for a worthwhile shopping spree, from high-end fashion outlets to traditional retailers.

🍣 Enjoy fine dishing with omakase sushi
Looking for a luxurious and delicious end to your trip? Top off your Osaka itinerary with omakase sushi.

❄️ And winter brings its own magic: snow-covered villages, hot-spring towns wrapped in steam, and serene landscapes that glow under soft white light ❄️🏔️.

caption:
Paris. Some cities we visit. Others never leave us. 🇫🇷🤍

Returning to Paris after so many years felt like finding a part of myself I had never lost. I lived here once, and walking through its streets again brought back memories, emotions, and a love that time never faded.

I love everything about Paris: its streets, the scent of fresh bread in the morning, its cafés, its art, and the beauty hidden in the simplest moments. Paris doesn’t need to try to be beautiful. It simply is.

A few days, far too few. I wish I could have stayed longer, reunited with friends, wandered through familiar streets, and captured beautiful memories during a photoshoot with my sister.

Being part of Paris Fashion Week with Flying Solo was already special. Sharing this experience with my sister, in the city of my heart, made it unforgettable.

Life has a beautiful way of bringing us back to places that once meant so much to us. And sometimes, we return not to relive the past, but to discover that some things never really left.

I leave with photographs, beautiful encounters, and a little longing for a city that will always feel like home.

À bientôt, Paris. Tu auras toujours une place dans mon cœur.

title: 2027년 정부 예산안이 나왔습니다 📊
why: 정부지원금 · 공개 표지·캡션 확보; 영상 편집 및 제작 방식 미판정

caption:
AI 기술의 발전은 중장년층에게 위기가 아닌 새로운 기회의 장을 열어주고 있습니다. 단순한 기술 활용을 넘어, 오랜 시간 축적된 '경험'과 '연륜'이 AI의 효율성과 만났을 때 비로소 대체 불가능한 경쟁력이 생겨납니다. 여기 중장년층이 도전하기 적합하고 실현 가능성이 높은 AI 부업 기술 5가지를 소개합니다.

첫째, AI 콘텐츠 에디터입니다. AI가 생성한 결과물은 팩트 검증과 인간적인 뉘앙스 보완이 반드시 필요합니다. 이는 문해력과 맥락 파악 능력이 뛰어난 중장년층에게 최적화된 영역입니다.

둘째, AI 기반 전자책 및 템플릿 제작입니다. 본인의 실무 경험을 AI를 통해 빠르게 지식 상품으로 만들 수 있으며, 이는 체력 부담 없이 지속적인 수익을 창출하는 자산이 됩니다.

셋째, 전문 분야 AI 학습 튜터입니다. 코딩 기술보다 중요한 것은 해당 산업에 대한 깊은 이해입니다. 20년 이상 현장을 지킨 전문가의 시각으로 AI가 올바르게 학습했는지 평가하는 역할은 AI 시대에 더욱 귀한 대접을 받습니다.

넷째, AI 자동화 마케팅 컨설턴트입니다. 많은 소상공인이 AI 도입을 원하고 있습니다. 이들을 돕는 외부 전문가의 수요는 공급을 초과하고 있는 실정입니다.

다섯째, AI 미디어 크리에이터입니다. 텍스트와 이미지를 포함한 디지털 콘텐츠 시장은 AI 생성물 위주로 재편되고 있어 시장성이 매우 큽니다.

혹자는 젊은 세대가 AI를 더 잘 다루지 않겠냐고 반문할 수 있습니다. 그러나 AI 툴의 조작법은 누구나 배울 수 있지만, 결과물의 품질을 판단하는 안목은 하루아침에 만들어지지 않습니다. AI는 생성을 잘하고, 중장년은 검수와 책임을 잘합니다. 이 둘은 완벽한 파트너입니다.

또한 이미 레드오션이라는 우려와 달리, 단순 사용자가 아닌 수익화 모델을 구축한 전문가는 극소수입니다. 4050세대의 업무 노하우와 결합된 커스텀 데이터는 AI가 흉내 낼 수 없는 독자적인 무기입니다.

마지막으로 기술 습득에 대한 두려움을 내려놓으셔도 됩니다. 최근 AI 트렌드는 코딩이 필요 없는 노코드 방식입니다. 우리가 일상에서 쓰는 언어로 명령하고 소통하면 됩니다. 소통 능력이 뛰어난 중장년층에게 진입 장벽은 그 어느 때보다 낮아졌습니다. 지금 당신의 경험을 디지털 자산으로 전환해 보시기 바랍니다.

문맥과 맞지 않는 이미지, 자막 구간, 화면 전환을

말 그대로 중소기업 성장을 지원하는 기관입니다.
정책자금, 마케팅, 인력양성 등 중소기업 성장을 위한 전반적인 사항을 지원합니다.
주요지원 업종은 제조, IT, 4차산업 등이며 지원사업에 따라 소상공인도 지원할 수 있습니다.

중소기업의 기술력, 성장성을 바탕으로 각종 자금과 지원금 혜택을 주고 있습니다.
*단순 도소매업이나 요식업은 지원하지 않습니다.

중소기업전문 종합지원 기관으로 창업자금, 시설자금 등

기술보증기금보다 좀 더 다양한 업종을 지원하며 매출과 수익성을 중요하게 봅니다.

<소상공인시장진흥공단>
자영업자, 소상공인, 전통시장 종사자 지원을 위해 설립된 곳입니 상시근로자 5인~10인 미만 사업장을 중점적으로 지원하고 있습니다.
성장기반자금, 일반경영안전자금 등을 지원하지만 위에 소개한 3개 기관보다 지원규모는 적습니다.

caption:
정책자금, 대출만 있는 게 아니에요 💡 오늘은 정책자금 3가지 종류, 한 번에 정리해드릴게요.

① 융자형 정책자금 (상환 O)

소상공인시장진흥공단(소진공) — 소상공인 대상, 저금리 정책자금의 대표 격

중소벤처기업진흥공단(중진공) — 업력 있는 중소·중견기업 대상, 소진공보다 한도가 큰 편

지역신용보증재단 — 보증서를 발급받아 은행 대출과 연계, 신용점수가 낮아도 가능성 있음 → 시중은행 대출보다 낮은 금리로 이용할 수 있는 게 가장 큰 장점이에요.

② 인증형 혜택 (상환 X, 메인비즈·이노비즈) 업력 3년 이상 중소기업이 받을 수 있는 인증이에요 (유효기간 3년).

이노비즈: 기술혁신형 — 특허·기업부설연구소·R&D 비중이 높은 제조·SW·바이오 기업에 적합

메인비즈: 경영혁신형 — 서비스·유통·전통 제조업처럼 경영 시스템이 탄탄한 기업에 적합 받으면 이런 혜택이 있어요.

보증기관 보증한도 확대 + 보증료율 감면

정기 세무조사 유예 (수도권 2년, 지방 3년)

공공기관 물품 구매 적격심사 가점

중기부 R&D 사업 신청 자격 및 가점 → 인증 자체는 대출이 아니지만, 있으면 정책자금 심사에서 확실히 유리해져요.

③ 비융자형 정부지원금 (상환 X) R&D 과제, 창업지원사업처럼 갚지 않아도 되는 지원금이에요. 대신 경쟁률이 높고 심사가 까다로운 편이라, 사업계획서 준비가 중요해요.

정리하면, 융자형 = 빌리는 돈 / 인증형 = 유리해지는 자격 / 비융자형 = 그냥 받는 돈 이렇게 성격이 다 다르기 때문에, 내 사업 상황에 맞는 걸 골라야 시간 낭비가 없어요.

내 사업엔 어떤 게 맞을지 정확히 확인하고 싶다면 댓글이나 DM 주세요 📩

Everyone is building AI for tech companies.

Pick one vertical, go deep, build the agent that handles their most painful workflow. 
One founder I know does this for independent pharmacies. $800/month. 60 customers. Do that math.

2️⃣ Idea 2: AI that fixes the output of other AI.
Most businesses use AI but get bad results because their workflows are broken. 
There’s a real business in being the layer between “we have ChatGPT” and “we actually get value from it.” 
Tools that monitor output quality, flag hallucinations, enforce brand voice. 
$200/month. Thousands of potential buyers.

3️⃣ Idea 3: Micro-PE wrapped in software.
Find a local business doing $500k/year with messy operations. Offer to run their scheduling and customer comms using AI, in exchange for 20% of revenue. 
That’s $100k/year from one client. Stack 5 of them.

Now, how do I find these?
→ Reddit: search “I wish there was a tool that”.
→ Job boards: if someone’s hiring a human to do it manually, that’s your opportunity.
→ Indie Hackers: internal tools founders built and never productized.
→ My own frustrations: if you’ve been a customer somewhere that felt broken, you already have the insight.

The best ideas aren’t creative. They’re obvious in hindsight.
You’re looking for a painful problem, an existing buyer, and a moment in time where building the solution is finally cheap enough to be worth it.
